items.aliasZh: 天青 · 天青色 · 传说汝窑的代表色
items.aliasEn: Tian qing · sky-clearing blue · the colour of Ru ware
items.histZh: 相传五代时柴世宗为烧造的瓷器定色，批了八个字：「雨过天青云破处，者般颜色作将来」—— 雨停之后云开的那一瞬，天是什么颜色，就烧什么颜色。宋代汝窑把这个颜色做到极致：釉面是淡蓝里带一点青灰，随光线变化，晴天偏青、阴天偏蓝，釉上还有细密的开片。汝窑烧造时间很短，传世器物很少，天青因此成了中国陶瓷史上最难复现的颜色之一。
items.histEn: Legend has it that the fifth-century emperor Chai Rong, asked to fix the colour of a new porcelain, wrote eight characters: where the clouds break after rain, that colour make it for the future. Whatever shade the sky is in the instant the rain stops and the cloud opens, that is the shade to fire. Song-dynasty Ru ware pushed it as far as it goes: a pale blue carrying a little blue-grey, shifting with the light, greener on a clear day and bluer under cloud, the glaze threaded with fine crackle. Ru ware was made for only a short period and very little survives, which is why this remains one of the hardest colours in Chinese ceramics to reproduce.
items.funZh: 今天想复现汝窑天青依然很难，因为它的呈色跟釉里微量的铁、窑内的还原气氛、以及冷却速度都有关，同一个配方放在窑里不同位置，出来的颜色就不一样。历代仿汝的作品非常多，但评论常说得刻薄：「仿其形易，得其色难。」
items.funEn: Reproducing Ru blue is still hard, because the colour depends on trace amounts of iron in the glaze, the reducing atmosphere inside the kiln and the rate of cooling; the same recipe fired in two positions in one kiln gives two different colours. Every century has produced imitations, and the usual verdict is unkind: the shape is easy, the colour is not.

items.aliasZh: 月白 · 月下白 · 名字是白，颜色是极浅的蓝
items.aliasEn: Yue bai · moon white · named white, in fact a whisper of blue
items.histZh: 名字听起来是白，其实是极淡的蓝。古人看月光落在白物上，看到的是带青的冷白，于是把这种颜色叫月白。明清的服饰、瓷器、漆器里都很常见：月白衫、月白绫、月白釉。它和「白色」在礼制上是两回事，属于一种有分量的素色 —— 素，但不等于随便。
items.histEn: The name says white; the colour is a very pale blue. Watching moonlight fall on something white, the eye reads a cool whiteness with blue in it, and that is what was called moon white. It appears throughout Ming and Qing dress, porcelain and lacquer: moon-white shirts, moon-white silk, moon-white glaze. In the ritual order it was not the same thing as white at all. It was a plain colour with weight behind it, plain but not casual.
items.funZh: 说到月白就绕不开《红楼梦》。书里丫鬟、仆妇、家常衣裳、丧服，月白反复出现 —— 晴雯病中穿的、夜里披的都有它。曹雪芹用颜色写身份和场合写得极细，月白就是那个不显眼、但到处都在的底色。
items.funEn: Moon white is inseparable from Dream of the Red Chamber, where it keeps appearing on maids, on ordinary household clothes and in mourning dress, on Qingwen as she lies ill and on whoever is up in the night. Cao Xueqin used colour to mark rank and occasion with great precision, and moon white is the unshowy shade underneath most of it.

items.aliasZh: 玄色 · 黑中带赤 · 上古礼服之色
items.aliasEn: Xuan se · black carrying red · the colour of ancient ceremonial dress
items.histZh: 《千字文》开头是「天地玄黄，宇宙洪荒」，玄指的是天将明未明时那种黑。严格说它不是纯黑，而是黑里带一点赤，也就是暗红。周代礼制里天子穿「玄衣纁裳」，上玄下纁：上衣是黑中透红的玄，下裳是黄中透红的纁 —— 一身衣服对应天地两色。
items.histEn: The Thousand Character Classic opens with heaven dark, earth yellow, the cosmos vast and wild. That dark is the black of a sky just before it turns light, and strictly speaking it is not pure black but black carrying red. Zhou ritual dress for the sovereign was a dark upper garment over a crimson-yellow lower one: black-with-red above for heaven, yellow-with-red below for earth, the two colours of the cosmos worn on one body.
items.funZh: 玄在中国色彩体系里位置很特殊：它既是最深的一档，又不像「黑」那样只表示没有光。道家的「玄」被用来指幽深而不可测的东西 —— 玄妙、玄机、玄学，词根都是这个颜色。「黑」是描述，「玄」是形容。
items.funEn: Xuan holds an unusual place in the Chinese palette: the deepest step, and yet not simply an absence of light the way black is. Daoist writing uses it for what is deep and unfathomable, and the words for subtlety, hidden mechanisms and metaphysics all grow from that root. Black describes; xuan characterises.

items.aliasZh: 靛青 · 靛蓝 · 从蓼蓝发酵而来
items.aliasEn: Dian qing · indigo · fermented from the indigo plant
items.histZh: 从蓼蓝、菘蓝这类植物里提取：把叶子沤烂、发酵，先得到蓝色沉淀，再做成靛饼，就是靛青。它是东亚和南亚最主要的蓝色来源，染布、染线，以及国画里的花青都从它来。荀子那句「青，取之于蓝，而青于蓝」，说的正是这道工艺 —— 从蓝草里提出来的颜色，比蓝草本身更深更浓。
items.histEn: It comes from plants such as polygonum indigo and woad: steep the leaves, let them ferment, take the blue sediment and press it into cakes. That was the main source of blue across East and South Asia for cloth, thread and the plant-based pigment used in Chinese painting. The line from Xunzi, that blue is taken from the indigo plant and is bluer than the plant, describes exactly this process: the colour drawn out of the plant is deeper than the plant itself.
items.funZh: 靛青染色有个反直觉的地方：刚从染缸里拎出来的布是黄绿色的，在空气里晾一会儿才慢慢变蓝 —— 因为靛蓝本身不溶于水，要先用还原剂把它变成可溶的靛白才能上染，上布之后再氧化回靛蓝。所以旧时染坊师傅判断火候，看的是那个「还没变蓝的颜色」。
items.funEn: Indigo dyeing has a counter-intuitive step. Cloth pulled from the vat is yellow-green and only turns blue as it hangs in the air, because indigo itself will not dissolve: a reducing agent must first convert it to soluble indigo white so it can enter the fibre, and oxidation afterwards brings the blue back. Which is why the old dye-house judgement of when the vat is right came down to reading the colour that has not turned blue yet.

items.aliasZh: 缃色 · 浅黄 · 缃本指浅黄色的丝帛
items.aliasEn: Xiang se · pale yellow · from the silk of that colour
items.histZh: 「缃」本来指浅黄色的丝织品，后来引申成这个颜色本身。汉乐府《陌上桑》写罗敷「缃绮为下裙，紫绮为上襦」—— 浅黄的下裙配紫色的上衣，是汉代人眼里很讲究的一套配色。古籍里的缃素、缃帙，指的都是这种淡黄色的书衣和书卷。
items.histEn: Xiang originally meant a pale yellow silk fabric, and only later the colour itself. The Han-dynasty ballad Mulberry on the Path describes the beauty Luo Fu in pale yellow patterned silk for a skirt and purple patterned silk for a jacket, which in Han eyes was a carefully judged pairing. In old texts the same word names the pale yellow cloth wraps and scrolls of a library.
items.funZh: 中国古代的书多用黄纸，一方面防虫，一方面淡黄不刺眼。于是「缃帙」「缃素」后来干脆成了书卷的代称。今天我们说缃色，说的是一种既被穿在身上、也被写在纸上的颜色。缃最常见的搭档是「缃帙」——浅黄的书衣。古书用缃色的布或纸做书套、书袋，于是「缃帙」慢慢就成了书卷的代称。一个颜色，最后变成了读书人的一个说法。
items.funEn: Books in China were commonly written on yellow paper, partly against insects and partly because pale yellow is easy on the eye, so the same word ended up meaning a library. To speak of xiang today is to name a colour that was both worn and written on. Its most common companion is the xiang-zhi, the pale yellow wrapper of old books. Chinese books and book bags were made with xiang-coloured cloth or paper, and the phrase for that wrapper gradually came to stand for books and scholarship. A colour quietly turned into a word for reading.

items.aliasZh: 胭脂 · 燕支 · 口脂与腮红 · 「胭脂」这个词可能来自人名
items.aliasEn: Yan zhi · rouge · lip and cheek colour
items.histZh: 用红蓝花取红，或以茜草、紫铆合制而成，是古代女子的面脂与口脂。《齐民要术》里记了从红蓝花里「杀花」取红的做法：先捣、再淘，用酸浆或草木灰水处理，把黄色素洗掉，只留红。工序繁，好的胭脂不便宜。
items.histEn: Made from safflower, or from madder and sappanwood together, it was the face and lip colour of Chinese women. The sixth-century agricultural manual Qimin Yaoshu records how to strip the red out of safflower: pound it, wash it, treat it with sour liquid or ash water to remove the yellow, and keep only the red. The process is laborious, and good rouge was not cheap.
items.funZh: 「胭脂」这个词的来源有两说：一说来自西域的燕支山，那里盛产红蓝花；一说来自匈奴单于正妻的称号「阏氏」，读音与胭脂相近。两种说法指向同一个方向 —— 红蓝花与这套妆容，是从北方和西域传进中原的。
items.funEn: Two explanations are given for the word. One traces it to Mount Yanzhi in the western regions, where safflower grew in quantity; the other to the title of the Xiongnu chieftain's senior wife, pronounced almost the same. Both point one way: the flower and the cosmetics made from it came into the central plains from the north and the west.

items.aliasZh: 藤黄 · 国画的黄 · 藤黄科树木的树脂
items.aliasEn: Gamboge · the yellow of Chinese painting · a tree resin
items.histZh: 从藤黄科树木树干上的切口流出树脂，凝成管状或块状，运到画室后再加水或加胶研磨使用。这种树主要长在东南亚，古代靠海路输入，所以国画家手里那一块藤黄是进口货，价格不低，用的时候要现磨。它明亮、透明，中国传统绘画里用来画花叶，常和花青、墨配合。它同时是一味中药，但有大毒，用量必须极小心。
items.histEn: The resin runs from cuts made in the trunk of trees in the garcinia family and hardens into sticks or lumps, which the studio then grinds with water or glue. Bright and transparent, it was used in Chinese painting for flowers and leaves, usually alongside indigo blue or ink. It is also a medicine in the Chinese pharmacopoeia, but a highly toxic one, and doses had to be watched closely.
items.funZh: 国画里常把藤黄和墨配在一起 —— 两者相调格外醒目，因此在旧时也被当作危险警示的配色。藤黄还有个麻烦：耐光性一般，长期见光的画上它会变淡。修复古画时，往往能在一幅画里看出哪一部分先「退」了。
items.funEn: Gamboge and ink are often paired in Chinese painting because together they are extremely striking, which is also why the combination was used for hazard warnings. Its weakness is lightfastness: it fades on paintings that see the sun, and conservators can often read off a picture which passages went first.

items.aliasZh: 石青 · 矿物蓝 · 与石绿同源
items.aliasEn: Shi qing · mineral blue · a companion of malachite
items.histZh: 由蓝铜矿研磨而成，是传统中国画里最正的蓝。它和石绿（孔雀石）常常在同一矿脉里伴生，一蓝一绿，性相近，古人用它们画山石与树叶。敦煌壁画里的青绿主要就是这两种矿物颜料：矿物色颗粒粗、遮盖强、千年不褪，所以今天的壁画上蓝和绿还亮着，而植物色的红早就淡了。
items.histEn: Ground from azurite, it is the truest blue in traditional Chinese painting. It occurs with malachite in the same ore bodies, one blue and one green and close in nature, and the two were used together for rocks and foliage. The blues and greens of the Dunhuang murals are largely these two mineral pigments: coarse, opaque and stable, so the blue and green are still bright today while the plant-based reds faded centuries ago.
items.funZh: 石青按颗粒粗细分等级：头青最粗最亮，用来铺大面；越细的二青、三青越灰，适合罩染。价格也按级走，头青最贵。所以一幅青绿山水里哪块用头青、哪块用三青，本身就透露了这幅画的成本。
items.funEn: Azurite was graded by particle size. The coarsest and brightest, head blue, was for large areas; the finer grades were greyer and suited to glazing, and the price fell with the grade. Which passages in a blue-and-green landscape got the top grade and which got the cheap one tells you what the painting cost.

items.aliasZh: 花青 · 靛花 · 与矿物色「石青」相对
items.aliasEn: Hua qing · vegetable blue · the counterpart of mineral azurite
items.histZh: 用靛蓝做成的国画颜料，属于植物色。它和石青虽然都是蓝，性格完全不同：石青是矿物，颗粒感强、遮盖、不透明；花青是植物色，透明，能渗进纸绢里，一加水就散开。画枝叶、水波、远山用花青，颜色薄、层次多；要厚重饱满，才上石青。
items.histEn: A painting pigment made from indigo and belonging to the plant colours. It is blue like azurite and nothing else like it: azurite is mineral, grainy, opaque and covering, while hua qing is transparent, sinks into paper and silk, and spreads the moment water is added. Foliage, water and distant hills call for the thin, layered plant colour; azurite comes out when weight is wanted.
items.funZh: 花青可以自己调：把靛蓝化开、滤掉渣、加一点胶防掉色。老手还讲究「放了几年的花青更好用」—— 新调的太跳，搁一段时间会沉下来，和水、墨配合得更顺。国画里这种对颜料要「养」的习惯，是化学性质之外的又一层经验。
items.funEn: Hua qing can be prepared by hand: dissolve the indigo, filter out the grit, add a little glue so it holds. Practitioners also insist that hua qing improves with a few years of sitting, since fresh it is jumpy and with time it settles into easier company with water and ink. The habit of keeping pigments as one keeps something alive is a layer of experience on top of chemistry.

items.aliasZh: 赭石 · 赭色 · 赤铁矿
items.histZh: 赤铁矿磨成的土色颜料，是人类用得最久的一种颜色。北京周口店山顶洞人的遗址里出土过赤铁矿粉和染过色的饰物，距今约一万八千年；欧洲的洞穴壁画也是一样。因为它到处都有、稳定、不褪色，赭石在几乎所有早期文明里都同时是颜料和象征 —— 红色常常被用来表示血与生命。
items.histEn: A colour ground from haematite and the longest-serving pigment there is. The cave site at Zhoukoudian near Beijing yielded ochre powder and dyed ornaments roughly eighteen thousand years old, and European cave painting tells the same story. Because it is everywhere, stable and permanent, ochre served nearly every early culture as pigment and as symbol at once; red was what stood for blood and for life.
items.funZh: 在中国画里赭石画山石、树干、老叶。它还经常和花青搭伙：赭石偏暖、花青偏冷，两色在纸上相调会得出一层很耐看的灰褐，用来画石头与远山。同一块土，一边是人类的第一个颜色，一边是水墨山水里的配角。
items.funEn: In Chinese painting ochre is for rocks, trunks and older leaves, and it is often paired with indigo blue: one warm, one cool, and together on paper they give a well-behaved grey-brown for stones and distant hills. The same earth is both humanity's first colour and the supporting player in ink landscape.

items.aliasZh: 竹青 · 竹子的青绿 · 一种带灰的绿
items.histZh: 竹叶与竹竿的颜色，是一种偏灰的绿。严格说竹竿才是青的，竹叶偏黄，所以「竹青」指的是新竹竿上那层带粉感的青绿。中国画里画竹多用水墨，竹青更多出现在设色作品、器物与织物上：明清都有竹青釉、竹青色素缎。它比草绿沉、比墨绿亮，是那种有灰在里面、看上去很安静的绿。
items.histEn: The colour of bamboo leaf and stem, a green with grey in it. Painting bamboo in ink is the default, so bamboo green shows up more on coloured works and on objects and textiles, including Ming and Qing glazes and plain satin of that name. Heavier than grass green, lighter than ink green, it is a quiet colour because of that grey.
items.funZh: 中国画里的绿其实没有几个：石绿是矿物、汁绿是藤黄加花青、竹青、苍绿。竹青往往是「汁绿」里再加一点墨调出来的 —— 画家不直接买它，而是调它。这个习惯很中国：颜色不是标准值，是配方和手感。
items.funEn: Chinese painting has surprisingly few greens: mineral malachite, a sap green of gamboge and indigo, bamboo green, and a dim blue-green for distance. Bamboo green is usually sap green with a touch of ink, mixed rather than bought. The habit is characteristic: a colour is not a standard value but a recipe and a feel in the hand.

items.aliasZh: 秋香 · 秋香色 · 浅黄绿的橄榄色
items.aliasEn: Qiu xiang · a pale olive yellow
items.histZh: 一种浅橄榄黄，名字取的是秋天草木的气味与颜色。明清的织物和服饰里很常见，《红楼梦》中不止一次出现秋香色的裙子与褂子，多用在日常、非正式的场合 —— 属于家常的那一档颜色，不是节庆上穿的。
items.histEn: A pale olive yellow, named for the smell and colour of plants in autumn. It is common in Ming and Qing textiles and dress, and more than one autumn-olive skirt and jacket turns up in Dream of the Red Chamber, mostly for everyday, unofficial occasions. It belongs to the household register of colours, not the festival one.
items.funZh: 中国色名有个特点：很多颜色是靠「东西」命名的，不是靠色相 —— 秋香、藕荷、竹青、月白、鸦青、丁香、猩红，都是先有一个具体物件或情境，再由它指代颜色。好处是想象空间大，坏处是极不精确：不同的人说的秋香色，未必是同一个黄。
items.funEn: Chinese colour names often come from things rather than from hue. Autumn olive, lotus pink, bamboo green, moon white, crow blue, lilac, scarlet: in each case an object or a moment came first and the colour is named after it. The advantage is room to imagine; the cost is precision. Two people describing autumn olive may not mean the same yellow.

items.aliasZh: 藕荷 · 藕合色 · 淡紫中含粉
items.aliasEn: Ou he · a pale lilac with pink in it
items.histZh: 藕荷色是淡紫里带一点粉，比丁香紫更淡、更暖。清代服饰与宫廷织绣里常见，也常用来形容春衫和女子的衣裳。名字取自荷花与藕，取的是那种粉中带紫、紫中带粉的中间状态 —— 两种颜色都不肯独占。
items.histEn: A pale lilac with pink in it, lighter and warmer than lilac proper. It appears throughout Qing dress and palace embroidery and is often used of spring jackets and women's clothing. The name comes from the lotus and its root, and takes the in-between state where pink leans toward violet and violet toward pink, neither of them willing to win.
items.funZh: 中国传统色里，淡紫系的名字几乎都能望文生味：藕荷、丁香、雪青、藤萝、紫棠。它们不像现代色卡那样有唯一的坐标，更像给一段明度和饱和度取了个名字 —— 所以看古典织物时，同一件东西有人叫藕荷、有人叫雪青，都说得通。
items.funEn: Nearly every pale violet in the Chinese palette tastes of its name: lotus pink, lilac, snow blue-green, wisteria, crabapple purple. They are not points on a chart the way modern swatches are, but names given to a stretch of lightness and saturation, which is why the same piece of old silk can be called lotus pink by one person and snow violet by another and both are right.

items.aliasZh: 暮山紫 · 出自《滕王阁序》
items.aliasEn: Mu shan zi · from the Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng
items.histZh: 王勃《滕王阁序》里那句「潦水尽而寒潭清，烟光凝而暮山紫」，写的是秋日傍晚，山色在薄雾与残光里从青转向紫的那一瞬。这个颜色后来被专门收进中国色的谱系里，是一种带灰的淡紫蓝 —— 不是花的颜色，是光的颜色。
items.histEn: In Wang Bo's preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng comes the line: the floodwater gone and the cold pool clear, the haze thickening and the evening hills purple. It describes one instant on an autumn evening as the hills turn from blue to violet in thin mist and failing light. The colour was later taken into the Chinese palette: a greyed pale violet-blue, not the colour of a flower but the colour of light.
items.funZh: 暮山紫这类颜色属于中国色的另一个来源：文人诗词。它们不来自颜料或织物，而来自某句诗给一个瞬间定的调子，后来有人把它「翻译」成一个色号。所以中国色的谱系里，既有染坊的手感，也有诗人的眼睛。
items.funEn: Colours like dusk mountain violet come from the other great source of the Chinese palette: poetry. They do not originate in a dye house or a mineral but in a line that fixed the tone of a moment, which someone later translated into a colour. The Chinese palette holds the feel of the workshop and the eye of the poet in the same list.

items.swEn: The red of the vermilion brush
items.aliasZh: 朱红 · 朱色 · 正红里偏橙的一路
items.histZh: 「朱」本指朱砂（硫化汞），后来凡是正红偏橙的那一路都叫朱红。它是中国最正式的红之一：宫墙、漆器、印章、判笔用的都是这一系。奏章上皇帝批的那句叫「朱批」，给犯人勾名的那支笔叫「朱笔」。「朱」在更早的文献里就是朱砂本身，颜色和材料是同一个词 —— 后来材料换成别的红，词却留了下来。这种「以材料名当颜色名」的情况在这份色卡里反复出现，朱、赭、黛、墨都是。
items.histEn: 朱 originally meant cinnabar, mercury sulphide; over time the whole orange-leaning branch of true red took the name. It is one of the most official reds in China — palace walls, lacquerware, seals and the judge's brush all sat in this family. A monarch's comment on a memorial was a 朱批, a vermilion comment; the brush that struck a name off a list was a 朱笔. In older texts 朱 is cinnabar itself: the material and the colour were one word, and when the material changed the word stayed. Naming a colour after its material happens again and again in this palette — vermilion, ochre, brow ink, ink.
items.funZh: 朱红偏橙，正红偏冷，两者在古代是有讲究的：朱连着官与法，正红连着喜与婚。屏幕上这个值是近似 —— 朱砂是矿物，磨出来深浅差得很远，没有唯一的色号。还有一层没人愿意细想的：朱砂含汞，是有毒的。古代长期点朱批的官员确实有过身体受损的记载，只是当时没人把账算到颜色头上。
items.funEn: Vermilion leans orange, true red leans cool, and the distinction carried weight: vermilion belonged to office and law, true red to celebration and marriage. The value here is an approximation — cinnabar is a mineral, and grinding it yields a wide range with no single colour number. There is also the part nobody likes to dwell on: cinnabar is mercuric sulphide, and toxic. Officials who spent careers with a vermilion brush do turn up in the records as unwell, though at the time nobody billed the colour.

items.aliasZh: 妃色 · 妃红 · 带橙的软红
items.aliasEn: Fei se · consort red · a warm soft red
items.histZh: 「妃」在古汉语里指配偶，也指地位高的女性。妃色是从「妃红」来的，说的是那种带橙、比大红软的红 —— 像胭脂晕开之后最浅的那一圈。妃红严格说不是某一种染料，而是一组描述：同一缸红，看染了几道、晒过几回。所以它在织物上从来不是一个精确的值，这也是现代色卡给它几种不同写法的原因。
items.histEn: In classical Chinese 妃 means a consort, a woman of rank. Fei se descends from 妃红, the softer orange-leaning red — the outermost, palest ring of rouge as it spreads. Fei red is less a dye than a set of descriptions: one vat of red, read by how many passes and how much sun. On cloth it was never an exact value, which is why modern charts give it several entries.
items.funZh: 这个色名最容易和「绯色」写混。绯偏冷偏紫，妃偏暖偏橙；在官服制度里，「绯」是一种品级，而「妃」形容的是脸色唇色。现代色卡把两个混在一起，得看上下文。它和「绯」的混用，在明清小说里就已经很常见了 —— 换句话说，这两个字的纠葛至少有几百年，不是现代人才搞不清。
items.funEn: It is easily confused with 绯色: that one is cool and heading toward purple, this one warm and heading toward orange. In the dress codes 绯 marked a rank, while 妃 described a face and a lip. Modern colour charts merge the two; context decides. The confusion with 绯 was already common in Ming and Qing fiction. In other words the two characters have been entangled for centuries; this is not a modern muddle.

items.aliasZh: 桃红 · 淡而不艳的粉
items.histZh: 桃花的红。春天桃花开时那种淡而不艳的粉，明清织物里常见，也用来形容少女的脸色。红花是从西域传进来的，唐宋以后才大规模种植。它的色素既怕碱又怕光，染粉的时候要拿酸把颜色沉下来，粉红因此比大红更难做匀，同一条裙子上有明显的深浅差是常事。
items.histEn: The colour of peach blossom. Pale without being loud, it turns up often in Ming and Qing textiles, and it is used to describe a young face. Safflower arrived from Central Asia and was only grown at scale from the Tang and Song onward. Its pigment is destroyed by alkali and fades in light, and making pink meant precipitating the colour in acid — so pink was harder to get even than red, and uneven depth across one skirt was normal.
items.funZh: 传统染色要得到桃红很难 —— 用红花染粉比染红还费料，要在碱性水里反复提、再往酸里沉，出的是那种一晒就褪的浅粉。所以桃红的衣裳在古代其实比大红娇贵得多。因为难做，粉红在很长时间里并不比正红便宜 —— 便宜的是那些用红花头道染出来的深红，末几道的浅粉才费料。
items.funEn: Getting peach pink from traditional dyes was harder than getting red: safflower needed repeated extraction in an alkaline bath and then precipitation in acid, and what came out was a pale pink that faded in sunlight. In practice, peach pink garments were more delicate — and costlier — than plain red. Because it was hard, pink was not the cheaper option for a long time: what came cheap were the deep reds off the first extraction, and the pale pinks at the end of the process cost material.

items.aliasZh: 海棠红 · 胭脂系 · 海棠开后
items.histZh: 取海棠花的颜色。海棠开后是深一点的胭脂红，所以叫海棠红 —— 比桃红浓、比胭脂淡。海棠在中国的园林里地位很高，唐宋以来写它的诗极多，色名就是从花来的。它和桃红、胭脂同属红的一路，区别在浓淡：海棠红比桃红深、比胭脂浅，正好卡在两者之间。
items.histEn: Named for the begonia. Once the flower opens the colour is a deeper rouge, so begonia red sits above peach pink and below straight rouge. The begonia held a high place in Chinese gardens and drew a great deal of Tang and Song poetry; the colour name came out of the flower. It sits in the same red family as peach pink and rouge, separated by depth — deeper than peach, paler than rouge.
items.funZh: 宋人写海棠有句「只恐夜深花睡去，故烧高烛照红妆」—— 半夜要点起蜡烛去看海棠。这个红在文人心里是什么位置，这句诗说得比色卡清楚。它是少数几个「以花定色、以色入诗」都成立的传统色：花名、色名、诗里的意象是同一个词。
items.funEn: A Song poet wrote of begonias: afraid the flower would fall asleep in the deep of night, he lit tall candles to look at its red dress. That line places this particular red better than any colour chart. It is one of the few traditional names that works as flower, as colour and as poetic image at once: one word doing all three jobs.

items.aliasZh: 绛紫 · 暗紫红 · 正式深色
items.aliasEn: Jiang zi · a formal dark purple-red
items.histZh: 绛是深红，紫是红蓝之间的色，绛紫是两者叠出来的暗紫红。它属于很正式的深色，唐宋以后常用于官服、帷幕和漆器。它属于所谓「间色」—— 由正色两两相配得来。古人对正色和间色分得很清，用什么色、用在什么场合都有规矩，绛紫这类深间色因此天然带着正式感。
items.histEn: 绛 is a deep red, 紫 the colour between red and blue; jiang zi is the dark purple-red of the two laid together. It reads as a formal, weighty colour, and from the Tang and Song onward it went on robes of office, hangings and lacquer. It counts as an intermediate colour, made by pairing two of the primary ones. The old system kept primary and intermediate colours firmly apart, with rules about what could be worn where, which is why a deep intermediate like this carries formality built in.
items.funZh: 「绛」在古书里单用就是深红。孔子时代有「红紫不以为亵服」的说法 —— 红紫系被当成贵重正式的颜色，不能拿来做贴身便服。孔子说过「恶紫之夺朱也」，说的是紫抢了朱的位置 —— 一个颜色被当成秩序问题来讨论，这在别的文明里不常见。
items.funEn: Used alone in old texts, 绛 simply means deep red. In Confucius's time there was a rule against wearing red and purple for everyday undergarments — the family was considered too important, too formal, for something worn against the skin. Confucius complained that purple was usurping the place of vermilion: a colour treated as a question of order, which is not a common move elsewhere.

items.aliasZh: 茜色 · 茜草红 · 古代主要红染料
items.aliasEn: Qian se · madder red · a staple dye
items.histZh: 茜草的根染出来的红。茜草在中国的使用极早，是古代最主要的红色染料之一 —— 比红花便宜，比朱砂耐久。茜草在中国古代是主要的红染料之一，根要长够年头才够用，所以种茜草是件需要耐心的事。它染出来的红偏暗、偏沉，不如红花艳，但耐洗耐晒，多用在日常衣裳和需要经久的织物上。
items.histEn: The red of madder root. Madder came into use very early in China and stood among the main red dyes — cheaper than safflower, more durable than cinnabar. Madder was one of the main red dyes in China; roots needed years in the ground before they were worth lifting, so growing it was an exercise in patience. Its red is darker and heavier than safflower's, but it stands up to washing and sun, which put it on everyday clothing.
items.funZh: 茜草根里真正能染色的成分极少，染深红要反复浸染很多次，一次只挂上很薄一层，全靠一层层叠出来。「茜」因此也引申成了层层累积、逐渐加深的意思。它在文献里出现得比在诗词里多 —— 一种染料的口碑，主要靠耐不耐用说话，这一点古今没变。
items.funEn: Only a tiny fraction of a madder root actually dyes. Building a deep red meant dipping again and again, each pass laying down a thin film, the depth coming entirely from accumulation. The word 茜 picked up that sense of layering and deepening. It appears in documents more than in poetry. A dye's reputation rested on whether it lasted, and that has not changed.

items.swEn: The colour of a first drink
items.aliasZh: 酡颜 · 酒后的红 · 一个状态色
items.aliasEn: Tuo yan · the flush of drink
items.histZh: 酡是喝了酒之后脸上的红。酡颜与其说是颜色的名字，不如说是状态的名字 —— 微醺时脸颊上那一层橘粉。这个色名出现在诗里的次数远多于出现在染坊账本里 —— 它不是一种能稳定染出来的颜色，而是先有了描述、后被色卡收编的例子。传统色名里由状态转成颜色的，还有酡、晕、热这一小撮。
items.histEn: 酡 is the red that comes to a face after drinking. Tuo yan is less a colour name than a condition: the orange-pink that appears on the cheeks at the first stage of being drunk. This name appears far more often in poetry than in a dyer's ledger: it was never a colour you could reliably dye, but a description the colour charts later adopted. A small group of traditional names made the same trip from condition to colour.
items.funZh: 古人写酒写得既刻薄又准确：「酡颜」是还没醉、但已经藏不住的时候。拿它当色名，等于把一个瞬间固定成了颜色。拿它做色名，等于把一个瞬间钉在色卡上。真按这个值去找布，多半找不到 —— 它本来就不是布的颜色。
items.funEn: Old writing on drink is both sharp and exact: tuo yan is the moment before drunkenness when nothing can be hidden any more. Making it a colour name means fixing an instant and calling it a pigment. Making it a colour name pins an instant onto a chart. Try to buy cloth in that value and you will mostly fail — it was never a cloth colour to begin with.

items.aliasZh: 绾色 · 旧绢色 · 偏棕的浅红
items.aliasEn: Wan se · a brown-leaning pale red
items.histZh: 绾的本义是把丝线盘起来、打结。作为颜色，指浅绛偏棕的那一层，常见于描述发色和旧绢。它更常出现在描写衣料和头发的句子里，说的是那种褪过几水、介于褐与红之间的旧色。古人对「新」和「旧」的色差很敏感，旧绢、旧衣自有一套颜色词。
items.histEn: 绾 originally means to coil silk and tie it off. As a colour it names the pale, brown-leaning end of crimson, used for hair and for ageing silk. It turns up mostly in descriptions of cloth and hair — the place between brown and red after several washes. The old vocabulary was acutely sensitive to new against worn, and old silk had colour words of its own.
items.funZh: 这个颜色很难定位 —— 同一本书的不同抄本里，「绾色」差得很多，有的偏灰、有的偏红。它算是凭手感传下来的色名：靠文字，不靠配方。它在不同抄本里差别这么大，也说明一件事：靠文字传下来的色名，一旦配方丢了，就只剩一个大概的方向。
items.funEn: It resists pinning down: different copies of the same book give 绾色 quite different values, some grey-leaning, some red. It is a name handed down by feel — through writing, not through a recipe. The wide spread between manuscript copies says something useful: once the recipe is gone, a colour name handed down in writing survives only as a direction.

items.aliasZh: 鹅黄 · 嫩黄带绿 · 唐宋常用
items.aliasEn: E huang · a tender yellow with green in it
items.histZh: 刚孵出来的小鹅身上那层绒毛的黄，嫩、亮、带一点绿意。唐宋诗词里用得很多，也用来指新柳和初春。这类嫩黄在染色上要靠槐花、黄檗这类植物染料，颜色偏淡、也容易褪，所以多用在春装、童衣和贴身衣物上，不太用于需要挺括正式的外袍。
items.histEn: The yellow of the down on a newly hatched gosling: tender, bright, with a hint of green. It appears constantly in Tang and Song poetry, and it also names new willow and the first weeks of spring. Tender yellows like this came from pagoda bud and amur cork, which dye pale and fade easily — so they went onto spring clothes, children's wear and undergarments rather than the stiff formal outer robe.
items.funZh: 古代给孩子做衣服、做襁褓爱用鹅黄，取的就是那个嫩字。要注意它在真实颜料里非常难做 —— 这个亮度接近屏幕能显示的极限，实际布料染不出来。古人对「嫩」这个评价很当回事：同样偏黄，嫩黄、鹅黄、柳黄是一档，缃色、秋香、黄栌又是另一档，分的是那种还没长开的感觉。
items.funEn: Garments and swaddling for infants were often made in gosling yellow, the whole point being tenderness. Note that this brightness is close to what a screen can show and beyond what cloth could take — no dye of the period reached it. Tenderness was a real category of judgement. Pale yellows like gosling and willow sit together; silk yellow, autumn olive and smoke tree yellow sit in another group entirely, and what separates them is the sense of something not yet grown out.

items.aliasZh: 杏黄 · 明清受管制的黄
items.aliasEn: Xing huang · a regulated imperial yellow
items.histZh: 熟杏子的黄，比鹅黄沉、比橙浅。明清两代它是受管制的颜色：杏黄与明黄接近，主要用于皇室与诏令。黄在五行里对应中央和土，一直是最受管制的颜色系。明清律例里，僭用黄色是要治罪的，所以民间的黄基本都往偏暗、偏红的方向走，避开明黄那一条线。
items.histEn: The yellow of a ripe apricot — heavier than gosling yellow, paler than orange. Through the Ming and Qing it was a controlled colour: close to imperial bright yellow, it was reserved largely for the court and for edicts. Yellow corresponds to the centre and to earth in the five phases, which kept it the most regulated colour family in the system. Ming and Qing law made unauthorised use punishable, so folk yellows drifted dark and red, steering clear of imperial bright yellow.
items.funZh: 黄是皇帝的色，所以杏黄在民间一直是「可以穿、但要有分寸」的黄。戏台上皇帝出场那件黄，按规制是明黄；杏黄往往给后宫或者仪仗用。这也是为什么传统色里的黄名目特别多 —— 不能碰的那一条线之外，需要足够多的说法来区分各种「合法的黄」。
items.funEn: Yellow belonged to the emperor, which made apricot yellow a colour commoners could wear only within limits. On the opera stage the emperor's robe is bright imperial yellow by regulation; apricot yellow tends to go to the inner court or the guard of honour. It is also why there are so many yellows in this palette: outside the forbidden line you need plenty of words to tell the legal yellows apart.

items.aliasZh: 琥珀 · 蜜黄到红褐 · 透光的暖橙
items.aliasEn: Hu po · amber · a translucent warm orange
items.histZh: 松脂埋在地下几千万年变成的石头，颜色从蜜黄到红褐都有。作为颜色名，指的是那种能透光的暖橙棕。琥珀在古代是贵重物：能做成珠子、印章、鼻烟壶，也能入药。同一块料，对着光看是暖橙，背着光看接近红褐 —— 色名取的正是透光那一面，所以它天然带着「亮」的意思。
items.histEn: Resin buried for tens of millions of years and turned to stone, running from honey yellow to red-brown. As a colour name it means that warm, light-passing orange-brown. Amber was a valuable material: beads, seals, snuff bottles, medicine. Held to the light a piece glows warm orange; held against it the same piece reads red-brown. The name takes the lit side, which is why brightness is built into it.
items.funZh: 琥珀能吸起小纸屑 —— 古人早就注意到了「琥珀拾芥」，这是人类最早记录下来的静电现象之一。颜色名取的就是它透光的那一面。它和西方同名的那个琥珀色（amber）并不完全一样 —— 中国色里的琥珀更沉、更偏褐，因为取的是器物而不是宝石。
items.funEn: Amber picks up scraps of paper. The phenomenon was noted long ago as 琥珀拾芥, amber lifting mustard seed, and stands among the earliest recorded observations of static electricity. The colour name takes the side of it that light comes through. It is not quite the same as the Western amber: the Chinese one sits deeper and browner, because it was read off an object rather than a gem.

items.aliasZh: 黄栌 · 取木质偏黄的一层
items.aliasEn: Huang lu · the yellow in the wood
items.histZh: 黄栌是一种树，秋天叶子红透，香山红叶的主力就是它。但「黄栌色」取的不是秋叶的艳红，而是它木质和果穗偏黄的那一层。它同时是一种染料植物 —— 黄栌的木材能染黄，古代叫「栌黄」，是黄色系里比较稳的一种。所以这个色名有实物依据，不只是拿风景比色。
items.histEn: The smoke tree turns a saturated red in autumn and is the mainstay of the autumn foliage around Beijing. The colour named after it, though, is not the leaf red — it is the yellow in the wood and seed heads. It is also a dye plant: the wood yields a yellow called 栌黄, one of the steadier yellows in the old palette. The name has a material behind it rather than being a landscape comparison.
items.funZh: 一个色名同时挂着最亮的秋红和偏暖的土黄，是因为古人看草木是一整年地看 —— 同一种树春天什么色、秋天什么色，都记在同一个名字底下。秋天去香山看红叶的人，多半不知道自己看的就是这个色名的来源 —— 一个词能同时挂住木材、染料、秋景三样东西。
items.funEn: One name covering both the brightest autumn red and a warm earth yellow makes sense if you watch a plant all year: the same tree in spring and in autumn is filed under a single word. Most people who go to see the autumn hills have no idea they are looking at the origin of this colour name — one word holding wood, dye and autumn at once.

items.aliasZh: 松花色 · 苔绿带黄 · 用在织物瓷器
items.aliasEn: Song hua se · a mossy yellow-green
items.histZh: 松花是松树的花粉，春天松林里一团一团地飘。松花色就是那种苔绿带黄的颜色，用在织物和瓷器上。松花在古人的用法里不只是颜色，还是吃食和药材 —— 松花粉可以做饼、可以止汗。所以「松花」这个词天然带着节令感：说起它，想到的是春天松林里那阵黄雾。
items.histEn: Pine pollen drifts through the woods in spring in loose clouds. Song hua se is the mossy yellow-green of it, applied in textiles and on porcelain. Pine pollen was food and medicine as well as colour: it went into cakes and was used to stop sweating. That gives the word a seasonal charge — say it and you are in a pine wood in spring, in a yellow haze.
items.funZh: 松花粉是要人爬上树去收的，一株成年马尾松能收到的花粉不到一两。拿这么费劲的东西给一个颜色命名，说明这个黄绿在古人眼里有多显眼。它也是少数几种「采集成本高到可以给颜色命名」的例子，同一类的还有藏红花色、胭脂色 —— 颜色名有时候记录的是一种劳动。
items.funEn: Collecting pine pollen means climbing the tree, and a mature masson pine yields less than an ounce. Naming a colour after something that hard to gather says how much it stood out. It is one of the few colours named after something expensive to gather, alongside saffron and cochineal. Sometimes a colour name is a record of labour.

items.aliasZh: 碧色 · 碧玉的青绿 · 诗词常用
items.aliasEn: Bi se · the blue-green of jade
items.histZh: 碧本指青绿色的玉石，后来泛指清亮透彻的蓝绿。诗词里的「碧」常和水、天、远山连在一起。碧和青、绿在中国色系里长期纠缠：碧偏蓝、绿偏黄，青则两边都沾。同一块玉，不同的人会叫出不同的名字，所以看古籍里的「碧」，不能按今天的色卡去对。
items.histEn: 碧 first meant a green-blue jade, then any clear, transparent blue-green. In poetry it attaches to water, sky and distant hills. Blue-green, green and blue have been entangled in this palette for a long time: 碧 leans blue, 绿 leans yellow, and 青 takes in both. The same piece of jade could get different names from different people, so a 碧 in an old text should not be matched against a modern chart.
items.funZh: 碧色在屏幕上显示得出来，在染料里却很难 —— 真实织物上的碧多是蓝与黄叠染出的青绿，比这个值暗、也更沉。这里的值只是屏幕近似。有意思的是，屏幕上能显示的这种亮碧，恰恰是实物上最难做出来的 —— 屏幕把碧变得比它本来的样子鲜艳了。
items.funEn: This colour exists on a screen but barely in a dye bath: on real cloth the 碧 of the poems was blue over yellow, darker and heavier than the value here, which is only a screen approximation. One irony: the bright blue-green a screen can show is the hardest version to make in real material. The display has made 碧 more vivid than it ever managed to be.

items.aliasZh: 石绿 · 孔雀石研成 · 重彩画的绿
items.aliasEn: Shi lv · malachite ground for heavy colour
items.histZh: 中国画里的矿物绿，原料是孔雀石，用法和石青一样要研漂分级。《千里江山图》里那层层叠叠的青绿山水，绿的那一层主要用的就是它。重彩画的做法是先铺石绿、再罩石青，顺序不能反 —— 石绿覆盖力强，垫得住底；石青透明，罩在上面才有那种发光的青。所以说到「青绿山水」，青和绿其实是两层工序。
items.histEn: The mineral green of Chinese painting, ground from malachite and, like 石青, levigated into grades. In the layered blue-green landscapes of the famous Thousand Li of Rivers and Mountains, the green layer is largely this. In heavy colour painting the order is fixed: green goes down first and blue over it, never the reverse. Green covers, so it can carry the ground; blue is transparent, and only over green does it glow. Blue-green landscape is literally two layers of work.
items.funZh: 石绿是重彩画里「盖得住」的颜色：覆盖力强，所以先铺石绿再罩石青，山才立得起来。它也是画上最先出问题的颜色之一 —— 胶一老化就粉化脱落。石绿也是青绿山水里最先出问题的地方：胶一老化就粉化，一碰就掉。修复这类画的时候，绿层往往比青层更需要小心。
items.funEn: In heavy colour painting shi lv is the one that covers, which is why a mountain is built green first and blue second, not the other way round. It is also among the first things to fail on an old painting: once the binder ages, it powders and flakes. It is also where a blue-green landscape fails first: once the binder ages it powders and comes away at a touch. When such a painting is conserved, the green layer usually needs the more careful hand.

items.aliasZh: 豆绿 · 宋代瓷器已有此名
items.histZh: 青豆的颜色，嫩黄绿。宋代瓷器和明清织物里都有这个色名。青色系在民间是最大的一支，因为靛蓝便宜、随处可得，套一层黄就换一个色名。豆绿、葱绿、水绿、柳绿之间的差别，在实物上常常只差半道染。
items.histEn: The colour of green peas — a tender yellow-green. The name appears on Song ceramics and in Ming and Qing textiles. The blue-greens were the largest family in ordinary life, because indigo was cheap and everywhere, and one pass of yellow renamed the cloth. Between pea green, scallion green, water green and willow green there is often half a dye bath of difference.
items.funZh: 传统染色里豆绿和葱绿很难分开 —— 两者都是蓝套黄，区别只在套的次数和黄的浓淡。名目繁多是好事也是麻烦：同一块布，不同的师傅会叫出不同的名字。条目多到这个程度，其实反映的是染坊的生意逻辑：名字越细，顾客越觉得讲究，加价也越容易说得出口。
items.funEn: In traditional dyeing, pea green and scallion green are hard to tell apart — both are yellow over blue, differing only in the number of passes and the strength of the yellow. A rich vocabulary is both a gift and a nuisance: the same cloth could get different names from different dyers. A vocabulary this crowded reflects the dyer's business logic: the finer the names, the more particular the customer feels, and the easier the surcharge is to justify.

items.aliasZh: 油绿 · 浓亮的绿 · 靠丝绸反光
items.aliasEn: You lv · a dense, bright green
items.histZh: 浓、亮、带一点油光的绿。名字说的是那种亮得像上了油的感觉。「油」在这里形容的是光泽，不是颜色本身。中国色名里有一小批是拿质感取名的：油绿、蜡色、银红 —— 它们描述的是表面反光的方式，色相反倒是次要的。
items.histEn: A dense, bright green with a sheen to it. The name says exactly that: bright as if it had been oiled. The oil here describes a sheen, not a hue. A small group of traditional names is built from texture instead: oily green, wax colour, silver red. What they describe is how a surface throws light; the hue comes second.
items.funZh: 这种亮度在天然染料里几乎做不到，得靠丝光 —— 蚕丝织物的反光会让颜色亮上一档。所以「油绿」这个词，很大程度上说的是丝绸，不是染料。这也解释了一个现象：同一种染料，做在棉布上就叫绿，做在丝绸上就叫油绿。
items.funEn: That brightness is nearly unreachable with natural dyes and had to come from the fibre: silk reflects light and lifts a colour a full step. So 油绿 describes silk as much as it describes a dye. It explains an oddity: the same dyestuff on cotton is simply green, and on silk becomes oily green.

items.swEn: The dark green of a crab shell
items.aliasZh: 蟹壳青 · 偏灰偏黑的青绿
items.aliasEn: Xie ke qing · a greyed dark blue-green
items.histZh: 螃蟹壳上那种暗青绿，偏灰、偏黑。名字里带的都是实物：蟹壳、鸽羽、麻雀头 —— 这类色名好用，是因为谁都不用解释。这类实物色名在口语里比在典章里活得久：染坊记账、布店报货、百姓挑衣服都用它，因为它不需要教育成本。代价是不够精确，同一句「蟹壳青」在南北两地能差出一档深浅。
items.histEn: The dark blue-green of a crab's shell, greyed and near black. Names of this kind point straight at an object — a crab shell, a pigeon's feather, a sparrow's head — and need no explanation, which is exactly why they work. Names of this kind lived longer in the mouth than in the statute book — dyers' ledgers, cloth merchants, people choosing clothes, all used them because they needed no teaching. The price is precision: the same crab shell green can differ by a step between north and south.
items.funZh: 蟹壳青在民间染坊里有个好处：它不挑染料，深蓝加一层黄就行，出什么算什么。所以它是最不出错的颜色之一，也是旧时百姓衣服上最常见的颜色之一。它偏暗、偏脏，所以在文人笔下很少见 —— 一个颜色能不能进诗，和它好不好看关系不大，和它代表什么关系更大。
items.funEn: In village dye houses it had one great virtue: it forgave. Deep blue with a pass of yellow, and whatever came out was crab shell green. That made it one of the safest colours to attempt — and one of the most common on ordinary clothes. Being dark and slightly muddy, it rarely appears in literati writing. Whether a colour can enter a poem has less to do with how it looks than with what it stands for.

items.swEn: The thin blue of a duck egg
items.aliasZh: 鸭卵青 · 白里透青 · 极浅冷色
items.aliasEn: Ya luan qing · a very pale cool blue
items.histZh: 鸭蛋壳的青色，白里带一层薄薄的青灰，属于极浅的冷色。鸭卵青属于「白里带色」的那一档，靠染料做不出来 —— 它更像瓷器釉色和丝织品天然的光泽。所以这类色名在瓷器谱录里出现得比在染坊里多。
items.histEn: The blue of a duck's egg: white with a thin wash of blue-grey over it, at the very pale end of the cool colours. Duck egg blue belongs to the whites with a colour inside them, and dyeing cannot get there: it is closer to a glaze or to the natural sheen of silk. Names like it appear more often in porcelain records than in dye ledgers.
items.funZh: 这类偏白的浅色说明一件事：古人看颜色不只看色相，还看它有多「嫩」。同样偏青，鸭卵青是壳，青碧是水 —— 差别就在浓淡和那一点灰。它和蛋青几乎是同一个色，区别只在前者更白。这种「半步之差」的成对条目在这份色卡里很多，说明当时的人确实分得出来 —— 至少天天和布料瓷器打交道的人分得出来。
items.funEn: Pale colours like this show that the old vocabulary tracked not just hue but freshness. Both are blue-leaning; one is the shell, the other is the water, and the whole difference is depth and a touch of grey. It and eggshell blue are nearly the same colour, one being paler. This palette is full of pairs a half-step apart, which says the people using them really could tell — at least anyone who spent their days with cloth and porcelain.

items.aliasZh: 苍青 · 带灰的蓝 · 天色将暮
items.aliasEn: Cang qing · a greyed blue at dusk
items.histZh: 「苍」是带灰的深色。苍青指天色将暮、山色转暗时那种发灰的蓝，古诗里「苍苍」多是这个意思。它在绘画里的用处是压住远处的山 —— 国画讲「远山如黛」，用的就是这种带灰的蓝。灰一加进去，颜色就往后退，这是中国画处理空间感的老办法。
items.histEn: 苍 is a deepened colour with grey in it. Cang qing is the greyed blue of a hillside as the light goes; the reduplicated 苍苍 in old verse usually means this. Its job in painting is to push distant mountains back. Chinese landscape painting speaks of distant hills like brow ink, and what does the pushing is grey: a little grey and the colour recedes. That is the old method for depth.
items.funZh: 「苍」大概是最难翻译的一个字：它可以指深蓝、灰绿、灰白，也可以指老迈（苍老）。苍青落在蓝灰这一格，但诗人用它的时候，往往同时带着天要黑了的意思。「苍」还常和年纪连用（苍老、苍颜），所以苍青这个颜色在文中出现时，往往同时带着天色和年岁的双重意味。
items.funEn: 苍 may be the hardest single character in this palette to translate: deep blue, grey-green, grey-white, or simply old. Cang qing occupies the blue-grey cell, but a poet using it usually means, at the same time, that night is coming. 苍 also attaches to age, as in the grey of years. So when the colour appears in a text it tends to carry both the hour and the years at once.

items.aliasZh: 铜绿 · 偏青的绿 · 器物色
items.histZh: 铜器生的锈，偏青的绿。和西方的铜绿一样是铜的化合物，中国画里也用，但更多出现在器物的描述里。它在中国色系里的位置和西方不同：西方主要拿它当颜料，中国更多是拿它当状态 —— 一件青铜器「生了铜绿」意味着年代和出土。所以它天然带着「旧」和「真」这两层意思，用它的时候很少是在说绿本身。
items.histEn: The corrosion on bronze, a green leaning blue. Chemically the same as Western verdigris; it appears in Chinese painting too, but more often it turns up when people are describing objects. Its place differs from the West's: there it was mainly a paint, here mainly a condition. A bronze that has gone green is old and it is genuine, which puts both age and authenticity into the colour. To use the word is rarely to talk about green itself.
items.funZh: 铜绿在铜器上是「坏」，在瓷器上却是「好」—— 宋代以后的窑口专门配铜绿釉去做仿古器。同一个化学反应，一边是腐蚀，一边是美学。铜绿在铜器上是「坏」，在瓷器上却是「好」—— 宋代以后的窑口专门配铜绿釉去做仿古器，用一种腐蚀的产物去模仿另一种腐蚀的产物，这件事本身就挺有意思。
items.funEn: On bronze it is damage; on porcelain it was desirable. Kilns from the Song onward formulated copper-green glazes specifically to imitate antiquity. One chemical reaction, corrosion on one side and aesthetics on the other. On bronze it is damage; on porcelain it was desirable. Kilns from the Song onward formulated copper-green glazes specifically to imitate antiquity — using one product of corrosion to imitate another, which is a strange thing to do on purpose.

items.aliasZh: 蔚蓝 · 明亮的天光蓝
items.aliasEn: Wei lan · a bright daylight blue
items.histZh: 蔚是草木茂盛，也是天空深广。蔚蓝指晴空那种明亮的蓝。它对应的是晴空和深水，所以在色系里属于「天色」那一支 —— 月白、霜色、苍青、蔚蓝，都是看天看出来的。这一支普遍比织物色亮，因为它们本来就没打算染在布上，而是用来写景、写时辰的。
items.histEn: 蔚 means lush growth, and also the depth and reach of the sky. Wei lan is the bright blue of a clear sky. It answers to clear sky and deep water, which puts it in the weather branch of the palette — moon white, frost, dusk blue, azure, all read off the sky. That branch runs brighter than the textile colours, because none of it was meant for cloth; it was for describing a scene or an hour.
items.funZh: 传统色名里蔚蓝是少数能对上现代高饱和屏幕色的，因为它描述的就是天光 —— 而天光本来就是亮的。大多数传统色取的是布料、器物和植物，都偏暗，所以整张色卡偏沉，蔚蓝是里面的例外。传统色名里蔚蓝是少数能对上现代高饱和屏幕色的，因为它描述的就是天光，而天光本来就是亮的。大多数传统色取的是布料、器物和植物，都偏暗，所以整张色卡偏沉，蔚蓝是里面的例外。
items.funEn: Wei lan is one of the few traditional names that matches a modern saturated screen colour, because what it describes is daylight, and daylight is bright. Most of the palette is drawn from cloth, objects and plants, all of which sit darker — so on the whole the traditional chart runs heavy, and this is the exception.

items.aliasZh: 宝蓝 · 明清颜色釉 · 织物也用
items.aliasEn: Bao lan · a strong blue in glaze and cloth
items.histZh: 宝石蓝，来自蓝宝石那种正蓝。明清瓷器颜色釉里有「宝蓝」一名，织物上也用。它在器物上是釉色名：明清颜色釉里有「宝蓝」一档，靠钴料发色，白瓷上要烧得很匀才好看。织物上的宝蓝则是靛蓝多次套染的结果 —— 两条完全不同的来路，最后共用了同一个词。
items.histEn: Sapphire — the straight blue of the stone. Ming and Qing glazes carry 宝蓝 as a named colour, and cloth used it too. On objects it is a glaze name: the Ming and Qing colour glazes include a sapphire grade coloured by cobalt, which on white ware needs a very even firing to look right. On cloth the same word comes from repeated indigo dips. Two unrelated routes ended at one name.
items.funZh: 宝蓝和藏青经常被拿来配。同一缸靛蓝，套染次数少的是宝蓝、多的是藏青 —— 所以这两个色在古代常常是同一批货的两头。两个来路的区别看边角就知道：釉上的宝蓝反光是玻璃的，布上的宝蓝反光是纤维的。同一句「宝蓝」，在不同行当的人嘴里，指的其实是两种东西。
items.funEn: It is often paired with 藏青, and with reason: from one indigo vat, fewer dips give sapphire blue and many dips give the darker navy. The two were frequently the same batch of cloth, described at either end. The difference shows at the edges: glazed sapphire reflects like glass, cloth sapphire like fibre. One phrase, and in two trades it means two different things.

items.swEn: A blue so deep it goes purple
items.aliasZh: 藏青 · 靛蓝染到最深处
items.aliasEn: Zang qing · indigo taken to its limit
items.histZh: 深到发紫的蓝。名字有说法认为来自西藏（藏地的青），也有人把「藏」解作深藏，指把颜色藏进去。现代纺织里它基本等同于深海军蓝，是制服、西装和中山装的常用色 —— 因为它耐脏、显正式，和什么颜色都能配。一个传统色名能一路用在今天的工作服上，在色卡里是很少见的。
items.histEn: A blue deep enough to turn purple. One reading traces the name to Tibet; another takes 藏 in its sense of hiding — colour tucked away inside. In modern textiles it sits close to a deep navy and is standard for uniforms, suits and the Mao jacket: it hides dirt, reads formal, and goes with anything. Not many traditional names survive into today's workwear.
items.funZh: 两种解释都说得通，这类色名的词源常常没有定论。能确定的是它在染色上属于靛蓝的最深处 —— 一匹布要反复浸染十几次，成本很高，所以藏青长时间是正式服装的色。它的两个词源解释一直没定论，但有意思的是两种解释都指向「深」—— 一种是地方的深，一种是程度上的深。色名的争议有时比色号还难解。
items.funEn: Both readings hold, and for names of this kind etymology often settles nothing. What is certain is where it sits in the dyeing: the deepest reach of indigo, a dozen-plus dips, and expensive. Which is why for a long time navy belonged to formal dress. Its etymology is still unsettled, and the two readings both point at depth — a depth of place and a depth of degree. A colour name can be harder to settle than a colour number.

items.aliasZh: 青莲 · 李白的号 · 紫偏蓝
items.aliasEn: Qing lian · violet-blue · Li Bai's studio name
items.histZh: 青莲是莲花的紫蓝色，也是唐代诗人李白的号「青莲居士」。作为颜色名，指紫色偏蓝的那一层。紫在中国的色系里一直有点特殊：它不在正色之列，但正因为难得，反而常被当成贵重的颜色。青莲这类偏蓝的紫比正紫好做得多，所以它在实际织物上出现得比「紫」更频繁。
items.histEn: Qing lian is the violet-blue of the lotus, and it was the Tang poet Li Bai's chosen name, 青莲居士, the Layman of the Blue Lotus. As a colour it names the blue-leaning side of violet. Purple has always been slightly apart here: not one of the primary colours, and precisely because it was scarce it often read as valuable. Blue-leaning violets like this one were much easier to make than true purple, so on real cloth they turn up more often than 紫 itself does.
items.funZh: 这个色名能流传下来，很大程度靠李白 —— 一个号带动了一个词。后来画家说「青莲色」的时候，多少还带着一点唐诗的气味。「青莲」这个词后来还进过地名和佛寺名 —— 一个色名走成了专有名词，这在传统色里不多，通常只有最常出现在诗文里的那几十个才有这个机会。
items.funEn: The survival of the name owes a great deal to Li Bai: one studio name carried a word along. Painters who later said 青莲色 were speaking, however faintly, in the scent of Tang poetry. The word also ended up in place names and temple names: a colour term that walked off into proper nouns. Only a few dozen names from this palette were common enough in poetry to earn that.

items.swEn: So dense it is nearly black
items.aliasZh: 紫棠 · 极深的紫红 · 戏服喜服
items.aliasEn: Zi tang · a purple-red near black
items.histZh: 极深的紫红，浓到近乎黑。「棠」取的是棠梨的木色，也可能只是形容浓艳。深到近黑的紫在古代是靠多次套染做出来的，成本极高，所以它更像是一种身份信号而不是日常色。喜服和戏服用它，是因为它远看沉稳、近看有东西可看，而不是因为它便宜。
items.histEn: A very deep purple-red, dense enough to read almost as black. The 棠 may refer to the wood of the wild pear, or may simply be there for the sound of richness. Getting a purple this close to black meant repeated dye baths and serious money, so it served as a signal of standing rather than an everyday colour. Wedding dress and opera costume use it because it reads sober at a distance and rewards a closer look — not because it was cheap.
items.funZh: 紫棠这样的深紫在古代很贵：紫色染料本就难得，深到紫棠更难得。所以它常出现在戏服和喜服上 —— 用量小、位置显眼，一眼看得出讲究。它在照片里常常直接读成黑色。这类「深色陷阱」在传统色里有一批，原因也简单：相机比人眼更早放弃暗部细节，而这些颜色本来就活在暗部。
items.funEn: A purple this deep was costly: the dye was hard to come by and the depth harder still. That is why it shows up on opera costumes and wedding dress — small area, prominent place, immediately legible as expense. In a photograph it often reads as plain black. A whole group of traditional colours falls into that trap, for a simple reason: the camera gives up on shadow detail earlier than the eye does, and these colours live in the shadow.

items.aliasZh: 丁香色 · 淡紫 · 花与香料同名
items.aliasEn: Ding xiang se · the pale violet of lilac
items.histZh: 丁香花的淡紫。丁香在中国既是花又是香料，色名取的是花那一层浅紫。丁香既是花也是香料，从南海输入，唐宋时是贵价货。拿它给颜色命名的时候，取的还是庭院里那株花 —— 所以这个色名带着很强的庭院感，和它的香料身份关系不大。
items.histEn: The pale violet of the lilac. The plant is both a flower and a spice in China; the colour takes the flower's lighter note. The clove is both a flower and a spice, imported from the south seas and expensive in Tang and Song times. The colour takes the garden plant rather than the trade good, which gives the name a strong sense of a courtyard and little sense of commerce.
items.funZh: 丁香花是四瓣的，所以古代有个词叫「丁香结」，用它形容心里解不开的小事 —— 一个花的名字先长成了情绪的词，再回头变成了颜色。淡紫系在中国色里条目不少：藕荷、雪青、青莲、丁香、藕色，说明当时的染坊确实能稳定做出这一档 —— 靠靛蓝加红花，比例稍变就是一个新名字，名目多也是这门生意的需要。
items.funEn: The flower has four petals, which gave rise to 丁香结, the lilac knot — a small thing in the heart that will not come undone. A flower's name became a word for a feeling, and then turned back into a colour. The palette carries plenty of pale violets — lotus pink, periwinkle, blue lotus, lilac, lotus white — which says dyers could hit this range reliably, using indigo with safflower. A small change in ratio bought a new name, and a crowded vocabulary suited the trade.

items.aliasZh: 雪青 · 淡紫偏蓝 · 清末民初常见
items.aliasEn: Xue qing · a pale blue-leaning violet
items.histZh: 一种淡紫偏蓝的颜色。名字里的「雪」不是白，而是洗淡的意思。它和丁香色、藕荷同属淡紫一系，区别主要在冷暖：雪青偏蓝、藕荷偏粉、丁香居中。这类细分靠肉眼就能分，在没有色卡的年代，全靠师傅的口传和布样本。
items.histEn: A pale violet leaning blue. The 雪 in the name does not mean white; it means washed out. It shares the pale-violet range with lilac and lotus pink, separated mainly by temperature: periwinkle leans blue, lotus pink leans pink, lilac sits between. The distinctions are visible to the naked eye, and with no charts to hand they lived in the master's speech and in swatch books.
items.funZh: 雪青在清末民初的民间染坊里很常见，属于「淡紫套色」的统称 —— 每家染坊的雪青都略有不同，因为都是靠蓝缸里随手套出来的。清末民初的染坊账本上，雪青出现的频率很高 —— 它是那个年代「不太张扬但也不沉闷」的标准答案，也是少数从染坊走进城市日常的传统色。
items.funEn: In late Qing and early Republican dye houses it was common, an umbrella name for the pale violets. Every workshop's version differed slightly, because all of them were improvised out of the indigo vat. In late Qing and Republican dye ledgers it appears constantly: the period's standard answer to not showy and not dull, and one of the few traditional colours that walked out of the dye house into urban daily life.

items.aliasZh: 藕色 · 极浅暖粉 · 与藕荷有别
items.aliasEn: Ou se · a very pale warm pink
items.histZh: 藕的断面那种白里透粉的颜色，属于极浅的暖粉。藕色取的是藕切开那一瞬间的断面 —— 白里透粉，还带着水汽。从食材来的色名在传统色里不多，但都相当准：因为大家都见过那个东西，不需要再加解释。
items.histEn: The colour of a cut lotus root: white with pink showing through, at the very pale end of the warm pinks. It takes the inside of a cut lotus root: white with pink showing through, still wet. Names taken from food are not numerous in this palette, but they are unusually precise — everyone has seen the thing, so no explanation is needed.
items.funZh: 藕色和藕荷色常被混用。一般来说藕色更浅、更偏白，藕荷带紫。这两个色名在织物上分得清楚，在文字里却经常混着写。它和藕荷色常被混用，但在织物上分得很清：藕色没有紫，藕荷有。这两个名字只差一个字，说的时候容易滑过去，写在货单上却是两回事。
items.funEn: It gets confused with 藕荷. Broadly, ou se is paler and whiter while ou he carries violet. On cloth the two were kept apart; in writing they merge constantly. It gets mixed up with lotus pink in writing, though on cloth the two are kept apart: one has no violet in it, the other does. A single character of difference, easy to lose in speech and impossible to lose on an invoice.

items.aliasZh: 象牙白 · 最「贵」的白 · 材料色
items.aliasEn: Ivory white · a colour named by its material
items.histZh: 象牙的颜色，白里带一点暖黄。它是传统色里最「贵」的白 —— 说的不是亮度，是材料。它是少数以材料命名的白 —— 别的白都来自天象和草木，只有它来自一种买不到的牙。这个差别在瓷器上尤其明显：象牙白的釉要偏暖、要哑光，和雪白的冷亮正好是对照。
items.histEn: The colour of ivory, white with a warm yellow in it. It is the most expensive white in the traditional palette, and the cost is in the material rather than in the brightness. It is one of the few whites named after a material; the others come from weather and plants, and this one from a tusk you can no longer buy. Porcelain shows the difference sharply: an ivory glaze wants warmth and a matte surface, the exact opposite of the cold brightness of snow white.
items.funZh: 象牙白、月白、雪白、霜色、鱼肚白 —— 传统色名里的白能分出十几种，区别全在冷暖与灰的程度。这套分辨力来自织物和瓷器：白瓷的品级，很多时候就是靠这点差别定的。它也说明传统色名的分辨力从哪来 —— 白瓷的品级很大程度上就靠这点冷暖差别定。能分出十几种白，是因为真的有人要靠它吃饭。
items.funEn: Ivory, moon white, snow white, frost, fish belly — the traditional vocabulary splits white into a dozen-odd entries, separated entirely by warmth and grey. That acuity came from cloth and porcelain: grading white ware often meant grading exactly these differences. It also shows where this vocabulary's acuity came from: grading white ware was largely grading exactly these differences in warmth. A dozen names for white exist because people were paid to tell them apart.

items.aliasZh: 雪白 · 与象牙白正相反
items.aliasEn: Xue bai · the cold end of white
items.histZh: 雪的白，冷、亮、带极淡的蓝。和象牙白正好相反：一个偏暖，一个偏冷。在织物上，白比别的颜色更难做 —— 所谓染出来的白，其实是漂得很干净。所以古代的白布料一直是身份的标志之一，穿一身干净的白比穿一身深色更费钱，也更难维持。
items.histEn: The white of snow: cold, bright, with the faintest blue. It is the exact opposite of ivory, one warm and one cool. On cloth, white is harder than anything else: a white textile is really a very well bleached one. White garments stayed a mark of standing for that reason — keeping a clean white was more expensive and more trouble than wearing a dark colour.
items.funZh: 纯白在屏幕上是 #FFFFFF，但真实的雪从来不是纯白 —— 它反射天空，所以永远带蓝或者带灰。色卡上这个值做的，就是把那个带蓝的白固定下来。雪白这类形容存在的意义，是把白的冷暖也分出等级来。同一个「白」，象牙白管家用，雪白管清冷，霜色管旧 —— 三个字，三种场合。
items.funEn: Pure white on a screen is #FFFFFF, but real snow never is: it reflects the sky, so it always carries blue or grey. What this value does is fix that bluish white in place. Names like snow white exist to grade the temperature of white as well as its purity. Four whites, four jobs: ivory for the domestic, snow for the cold, frost for the aged.

items.aliasZh: 霜色 · 比雪白灰一点 · 一色双关
items.aliasEn: Shuang se · frost · grey against snow white
items.histZh: 霜的青白色，比雪白灰一点。用来形容清晨、鬓发，以及旧纸。霜色介于白与灰之间，最接近旧纸和旧绢本身。写旧书、旧画、旧衣裳的时候用它，一句话就把年代感交代了，不需要另外说「发黄」或者「褪色」。
items.histEn: The blue-white of frost, a touch greyer than snow. It describes early morning, greying hair, and old paper. Between white and grey, frost is closest to old paper and old silk as they actually are. Used of a book, a painting or a garment it carries the sense of age in one word, with nobody needing to add yellowed or faded.
items.funZh: 霜色常和霜的两种含义一起用：既是颜色，也是年纪（霜鬓）。中文色名里这种一色双关非常多，读的时候得看上下文。它也是中国色里少见的、几乎不带感情色彩的中性色 —— 大多数传统色名都连着情绪（酡颜、霜鬓），霜色只连着时间。
items.funEn: The name works two ways at once, as colour and as age — 霜鬓, temples going frosty. Puns of this kind run all through the Chinese colour vocabulary, and reading them requires the sentence around them. It is also one of the few near-neutral entries, almost free of feeling. Most of these names carry emotion — a flushed face, frosty temples; frost holds only time.

items.aliasZh: 鱼肚白 · 偏暖偏粉的白 · 黎明色
items.aliasEn: Yu du bai · a warm, faintly pink white
items.histZh: 鱼翻过来露出肚皮的那一层白，偏暖、偏粉。也用来指天快亮时东方那一条白。它在实际用色里更多是形容天光而不是织物 —— 「东方既白」说的就是那一段。古人写日出往往不写太阳，写的是天亮之前的这个色，这是汉诗里很常见的手法。
items.histEn: The white of a fish turned over to show its belly: warm, faintly pink. It also names the band of light in the east just before sunrise. In practice it describes daylight more than cloth: the eastern sky going white, the moment before sunrise. Poems about dawn often skip the sun and describe this colour instead, which is a common move in Chinese verse.
items.funZh: 鱼肚白是传统色名里少见的、和食物有关的白 —— 别的几个白都来自自然（月、雪、霜），只有它来自集市。用它形容黎明，是因为那一刻的天色真的像鱼腹。它是传统色名里少见的、和食物有关的白 —— 别的几个白都来自天象（月、雪、霜），只有它来自集市。用它形容黎明，是因为那一刻的天色真的像鱼腹。
items.funEn: It is the rare white in this vocabulary that comes from food. The others arrive from nature, from moon and snow and frost; this one comes from the market. Applied to dawn, it works because at that hour the sky really does look like the inside of a fish. It is the rare white in this vocabulary that comes from food. The others arrive from the sky, from moon and snow and frost; this one comes from the market. Applied to dawn, it works because at that hour the sky really does look like the inside of a fish.

items.swEn: Grey after the water goes in
items.aliasZh: 墨色 · 墨分五色 · 一个区间
items.aliasEn: Mo se · ink · a range, not a value
items.histZh: 墨的颜色。但注意它落在这一格偏灰蓝的浅色上 —— 墨分五色，浓淡不同，「墨色」常常指研开之后的那一层中灰，而不是墨块的漆黑。它在画论里指的是一整套明度，不是一个值。同一块墨，兑水多少、落在生宣还是熟纸上，出来的东西完全不同 —— 所以「墨色如何」在中国画里是对技术的评价，不是对颜色的评价。
items.histEn: The colour of ink — but note where it lands: a light grey-blue, not the black of the stick. 墨分五色, ink divides into five colours by dilution, which means 墨色 usually names the middle grey of a wash rather than the solid block. In painting theory it names a whole range of values rather than one reading. The same ink stick gives something entirely different depending on how much water it meets and whether the paper is sized. To judge someone's ink colour is to judge their technique, not their palette.
items.funZh: 中国画里说墨是「墨分五色」，这话的意思不是墨有五种颜色，而是同一块墨靠水和纸能出五个层次。所以「墨色」在画论里不是一个值，是一个区间。所以「墨色」这个词在画论里从来不配一个色号 —— 它是这整份色卡里唯一一个明确表示「我指的是一段区间」的条目，这也算是它自己的性格。
items.funEn: The phrase does not mean ink has five colours. It means one ink stick, with water and paper, yields five levels. In painting theory 墨色 is a range, not a reading. Which is why no colour number will ever be attached to it: among all the entries here it is the one that openly means a range. That is its character.

items.swEn: Black with blue going through it
items.aliasZh: 玄青 · 玄是黑中带红 · 织物漆器
items.histZh: 玄是黑中带红，青是蓝绿，玄青是黑里透蓝的深色，常见于织物与漆器。这类深色在织物上其实是套染的结果：靛蓝打底，再套一遍红或者黄，往哪个方向走就出玄或者出青。所以古代染坊的深色系是一个连续谱，名字只是谱上的刻度。
items.histEn: 玄 is black with red in it, 青 is blue-green; xuan qing is the deep colour of black with blue running through. It appears on cloth and on lacquer. Deep colours like this on cloth are really overdyes: indigo for the ground, then a pass of red or yellow, and the direction taken decides whether it lands near black or near blue. The dyer's dark range was a continuum, and the names are tick marks on it.
items.funZh: 有个常被认错的点：《千字文》开头「天地玄黄」里的「玄」是黑红，不是黑。中国色里的黑从来不只是一个黑 —— 玄、墨、乌、黛、鸦青，各偏一个方向。《千字文》开头「天地玄黄」里的「玄」是黑中带红，不是纯黑 —— 这一点常被读错。中国色里的黑从来不只是一个黑：玄、墨、乌、黛、鸦青，各偏一个方向。
items.funEn: One common misreading: the 玄 of 天地玄黄, the opening of the Thousand Character Classic, is a red-black, not a plain black. Black in this vocabulary is never one thing — 玄, 墨, 乌, 黛, 鸦青 all lean somewhere different. The 玄 of 天地玄黄, the opening of the Thousand Character Classic, is a red-black rather than a plain one, which is widely misread. Black here is never one thing: 玄, 墨, 乌, 黛, 鸦青 all lean somewhere different.

items.aliasZh: 黛 · 青中带紫的深色 · 也指女子
items.aliasEn: Dai · a purple-leaning dark, and a word for women
items.histZh: 黛是古代画眉用的颜料，本是一种青黑色的矿石。作为颜色名，指青中带紫的深色。画眉是古代女性日常里少数需要专门工具和材料的事，所以「黛」这个词连着的是一整套动作：描、晕、卸。它后来引申成女子的代称，和使用场景是分不开的。
items.histEn: Dai was the pigment used to paint eyebrows, originally a blue-black mineral. As a colour name it means the dark that carries violet inside its blue. Painting the brows was one of the few parts of a woman's day that needed special tools and materials, so the word carries a sequence with it: outline, soften, take off. That it later became a word for women is not separable from that daily use.
items.funZh: 「六宫粉黛无颜色」里的黛就是眉色 —— 拿画眉的颜料当颜色的通称。它后来还引申成了女子的代称：一个色名最后长成了人物。「黛」也进过地名，走的还是同一个意思：远看发青的深色。一个从化妆品来的词，最后落在山水上，这种转移在色名里不多见。
items.funEn: In the line about the palace women whose powder and dai lost their colour, dai means the brow. The pigment became a general word for the colour, and then a word for the women themselves — a colour name that ended up as a person. It also entered place names, still meaning the same thing: a dark that looks blue from a distance. A word that started in cosmetics and ended up on hills — a transfer that does not happen often.

items.histZh: 《说文解字》说「绛，大赤也」，是比朱更深一层的红。先秦到汉代，绛是礼服的正色之一，《论语》里那句「红紫不以为亵服」，说的正是这一类深红不能拿来当便服穿。后来绛从衣冠上慢慢退下来，留在了别的地方 —— 绛帐、绛纱。屏幕上的深红只是近似值，血色矿物与植物染料出的绛要沉得多。
items.histEn: The Shuowen Jiezi, the second-century Chinese dictionary, glosses jiang as the great red — a shade deeper than vermilion. Through the Qin and Han it was one of the proper colours of ceremonial dress, and the red that the Analects refuses to see worn as casual clothing belongs to this deep family. The word later withdrew from robes and settled elsewhere: into place names, and into the jiangzhang, the crimson curtain of a lecture hall. What you see on a screen is only an approximation; the colour that came out of mineral and plant dyes was considerably heavier.
items.funZh: 今天还留在汉语里的「绛」，多半跟讲学有关：东汉马融讲学时设绛色纱帐，前面授徒、后面列女乐，于是「绛帐」慢慢成了师门的代称。一个颜色，最后变成了一句尊称。
items.funEn: What survives of the word today is mostly about teaching. The Eastern Han scholar Ma Rong lectured behind a crimson gauze curtain, pupils in front and a small orchestra of women behind — and jiangzhang, the crimson tent, became a byword for a teacher's hall. A colour quietly turned into a term of respect.

items.histZh: 绯是比绛浅、比桃红正的红。唐代的官服按品级配色，四品、五品穿绯，所以「绯衣」在唐诗里常常就等于中层官员本人。白居易写「江州司马青衫湿」，青衫是八品九品的服色 —— 他那时被贬，穿的正是最低的那一档，才衬得那句湿透了。屏幕上的绯是按唐代服色复原的近似值，真丝上染出来的要更暖一点。
items.histEn: Fei is lighter than jiang and truer than peach — the red of a middle-rank official. Tang court dress was colour-coded by rank, and grades four and five wore fei, which is why scarlet robes in Tang poetry usually stand for the officials themselves. Bai Juyi, exiled and demoted, wrote of his blue-green robe soaked with tears; blue-green was the colour of the eighth and ninth grades, the lowest rungs, and that is what makes the line land. The value here is a reconstruction from Tang regulations, not a measurement.
items.funZh: 「绯闻」这个词跟衣服有关。唐代新科进士要在长安的曲江边宴饮，叫「曲江宴」，其中有一项是去名园里折花，人骑马、花插帽，热闹得满城围观；后来这类体面场合的是非口舌被记成「绯闻」，绯字就这么从官服跑到了八卦里。
items.funEn: The modern Chinese word for scandal carries this colour inside it. Newly passed imperial examinees feasted by Qujiang in Chang'an and rode out to pick flowers from famous gardens, caps decked, crowds watching — and the gossip that attached to such conspicuous occasions kept the word fei, so that a rank badge of office ended up doing duty for tabloid talk.

items.histZh: 丹本来是矿物名，就是丹砂，也就是朱砂。因为颜色硬、不褪，古人把它当成最靠得住的红：漆器上用它，印章上用它，道士炼丹炼的也是它 —— 「丹」这个字后来干脆成了丹药、丹方的丹。屏幕上的丹红比真朱砂稍亮，磨得极细的朱砂其实偏暗、带一点橙。
items.histEn: Dan began as the name of a mineral — cinnabar, the ore that yields vermilion. Because the colour was hard, opaque and did not fade, the Chinese world treated it as the most dependable of reds: on lacquer, in seals, and in the crucibles of Daoist alchemists, whose pursuit of elixirs took its name from the same word. On a screen this red runs brighter than the real thing; cinnabar ground very fine is darker and tips slightly toward orange.
items.funZh: 「丹青」之所以能代指绘画，就是因为这两个字本身是两种最耐久的颜料：丹是朱砂，青是石青。古人画画先备这两样，所以「丹青」不是「红色和蓝色」，而是「画」这件事本身。后来它又引申出「丹青不知老将至」这类说法，颜料变成了志业。
items.funEn: The classical term for painting is made of two pigment names: dan, cinnabar, and qing, azurite. They were the two most durable colours in a painter's kit, so the pair came to stand not for red and blue but for the craft itself — and then, by extension, for a lifelong vocation that outlasts the awareness of growing old.

items.histZh: 缇是橙红偏黄的一档，《说文》解作「帛丹黄色」，就是染成丹黄色的丝帛。它在史书里最出名的一次出场跟颜色关系不大：汉代执金吾属下有「缇骑」，穿缇色号衣的骑兵，负责巡街、捕人，后来「缇骑」成了明代锦衣卫的别称。屏幕上的缇色是据文献复原的近似值。
items.histEn: Ti sits between orange and yellow; the Shuowen describes it as silk dyed the colour of cinnabar-yellow. Its most famous appearance in the histories has little to do with colour: the Han capital police included the tiqi, riders in ti-coloured uniforms who patrolled the streets and made arrests. The name outlived the office by well over a thousand years, resurfacing as a byword for the Ming secret police. The value shown is a reconstruction from textual description.
items.funZh: 「缇萦救父」是中国法制史上常被提起的一段：汉文帝时少女缇萦上书，愿没入官婢替父亲赎刑，文帝因此下诏废除肉刑。缇萦的「缇」跟缇色本来没有关系，但一个颜色和一个名字就这样叠在了一起，讲了两千年。
items.funEn: Chinese legal history keeps returning to a girl named Ti Ying, who petitioned Emperor Wen of Han offering to become a state slave if her father's corporal punishment could be commuted — and the emperor duly abolished mutilation. Her given name has nothing to do with the colour, but the two have been pronounced and remembered together for two thousand years.

items.histZh: 檀色取自檀木的心材，是偏红偏灰的浅赭。它在中国色名里不算最古老的一批，更多是随家具和香料进来的：檀香木从南方与海外输入，紫檀、白檀各按材色得名，檀色于是成了介于赭石与绾色之间的一档。屏幕上的檀色按旧家具的材色取样，实际木料随年份变深，差异不小。
items.histEn: Sandal takes its name from the heartwood of the sandalwood tree — a reddish, slightly grey light russet. It is not among the oldest Chinese colour words; it arrived with the timber and the incense trade, as sandalwood came in from the south and from overseas and the various species were named for the colour of their wood. Sandal settled into the slot between ochre and the muted reddish brown called wanse. The sample here is taken from aged furniture; real timber darkens considerably with time.
items.funZh: 檀色最容易被误认成「紫色」的近亲，其实它一点也不紫。真正带紫的是紫檀 —— 同一种树按心材与边材分，颜色能差出很远。古人把「檀」既当香也当料，一块木头同时供在佛前和做成桌子，是很常见的事。
items.funEn: Sandal is easily mistaken for a relative of purple, and it is not — the purple belongs to rosewood, and the difference runs through the same trade. Whether a tree was cut for incense or for furniture was largely a question of which part of it you were holding, and a single log might end up both on an altar and in a table.

items.histZh: 赪就是赤，《诗经》里「鲂鱼赪尾」写鱼尾发红，后来多用来形容人脸红 —— 「赪颜」就是涨红了脸。它不是一种颜料，而是古人对「红到什么程度」的描写：比丹浅，比普通的赤多一点血气。今天在屏幕上给它一个色号，本身就有点勉强，它是从文字里取出来的颜色。
items.histEn: Cheng simply means red, but a particular red. The Book of Songs uses it of a bream's flushed tail, and later writers use it of a face: to be cheng-faced is to be red with embarrassment or anger. It names no pigment, only a degree of redness — lighter than cinnabar, warmer than an ordinary red, carrying blood in it. Assigning it a hex value is an act of translation from literature rather than from matter.
items.funZh: 这类「没有实物、只有描述」的颜色在传统色名里不少：赪、酡、缊、皓，都更像是古人对颜色程度的形容，而不是能拿来染布的方子。把它们一一落成色号，多少有点把形容词当成名词在用 —— 但这也是传统色好玩的地方。
items.funEn: Chinese colour vocabulary contains a whole class of words that name no object at all — cheng, tuo, yun, hao — descriptions of degree rather than recipes for dye. Turning each of them into a hex value is arguably treating an adjective as a noun. It is also, frankly, the most entertaining part of the exercise.

items.histZh: 银红是红里掺了大量白的那种粉，比水红更淡、更灰一点，名字里的「银」指的是它那层泛白的调子。明清小说里女子的衫子常是银红，《红楼梦》里出现过好几次，多用来配月白、配葱绿。屏幕上的这一档偏亮，旧丝绸上的银红因为染料和岁月，往往更沉。
items.histEn: Silver pink is a red carrying a great deal of white — paler and greyer than the shade called water-red, the silver in the name naming that washed-out cast. In Ming and Qing fiction, young women's jackets are very often silver pink, and Dream of the Red Chamber dresses its heroines in it repeatedly, usually set against moon-white or scallion green. This value runs bright; on aged silk, dye and time pull it much deeper.
items.funZh: 传统色里有一套「以物命名」的粉：水红、银红、藕合、杨妃、海棠。它们的差别不在色相环上隔多远，而在掺白多少和偏冷偏暖。旧时染坊靠口传和样布对色，同一句「银红」到不同染坊手里，出来的深浅可以差出一档。
items.funEn: Traditional pinks come in a series named after things: water-red, silver pink, lotus-root, imperial consort, crabapple. What separates them is less hue than how much white has been let in and whether the result runs cool or warm. Old dye houses matched colours by swatch and word of mouth rather than by formula, so the same instruction could produce two noticeably different pinks in two different workshops.

items.histZh: 榴红取自石榴花。石榴原产波斯一带，汉代经西域传入，因为多子，很快成了婚嫁与多子的吉祥物，榴红色也带着这一层意思，常出现在嫁衣、帐幔和年画上。这个红比朱红偏橙、比妃色更饱和。屏幕上的榴红按花期盛放时的花冠取色，实际花瓣受光不同，深浅差得不小。
items.histEn: Pomegranate red is taken from the flower. The tree came to China from Persia by way of the western regions in the Han period, and because its fruit is dense with seeds it quickly became a token of fertility and marriage; the colour carried that meaning onto bridal clothes, bed hangings and New Year prints. It runs more orange than vermilion and more saturated than the shade called imperial consort. This sample comes from a flower at full bloom; real petals vary widely with the light.
items.funZh: 石榴籽多，古人由此造出「榴开百子」的吉利话，榴红色因此常常直接画在婚嫁的器物上，而不是当颜料用。有意思的是它很少进画谱：植物染料染不出这么正的榴红，画上去的多半是朱砂或银朱，颜色名字管的是「意思」，不是「配方」。
items.funEn: Because the fruit is packed with seeds, the pomegranate gave Chinese a stock blessing — one pomegranate opens into a hundred sons — and the colour was accordingly painted onto wedding objects rather than used as an artist's pigment. Tellingly, it barely appears in painting manuals: vegetable dyes could not reach that particular red, so what was actually laid down was cinnabar or vermilion. The name governed meaning, not recipe.

items.histZh: 姜黄既是香料名也是染料名，色取自姜科植物姜黄的根茎。它在中国和印度都用了很久，佛教僧衣的「袈裟色」里就有它的一份 —— 因为便宜、染得牢，又不算鲜艳，正合戒律里「不以色媚人」的分寸。屏幕上的姜黄偏亮，实际染出的布是带土味的黄，放久会转褐。
items.histEn: Turmeric is at once a spice and a dye, the colour taken from the rhizome of a plant in the ginger family. It has been in use in China and India for a very long time, and it has a share in the yellow-browns of Buddhist monastic robes: cheap, fast-dyeing, never brilliant, and therefore suited to a rule that asks a monk not to be seductive in dress. This value runs bright; cloth dyed with it comes out earthier and browns with age.
items.funZh: 姜黄染出的黄有个出名的毛病：怕光。挂在墙上的姜黄染纺织品放上几年，受光的一面会明显褪成浅褐，没晒到的一面还黄着 —— 修复师常靠这个反差判断一件织物当年是怎么挂的、哪一面朝外。
items.funEn: Turmeric yellow has a famous weakness: light. Hang a turmeric-dyed textile on a wall for a few years and the exposed side fades markedly toward pale brown while the covered side stays yellow. Conservators read exactly that contrast to work out how a piece was once displayed and which face was turned outward.

items.histZh: 栀黄是拿栀子果实染的。栀子是秦汉以来最常用的黄色染料之一，染出的黄带一点暖橙，比藤黄稳、比姜黄亮。马王堆出土的西汉织物里就有栀子染的黄，说明它在两千年前已经是成熟的工艺。屏幕上的栀黄按新染的样布取色，实际织物随年份会转暗发褐。
items.histEn: Gardenia yellow is dyed from the fruit of the gardenia. It was among the most widely used yellow dyes from the Qin and Han onward, warm rather than acid, steadier than gamboge and brighter than turmeric. Yellow silks dyed with gardenia were recovered from the Western Han tomb at Mawangdui, which places it as a mature craft two thousand years ago. This sample reflects freshly dyed cloth; textiles darken and brown over time.
items.funZh: 栀子入药、入香、也入染缸，一身多用。它染出的黄在旧文献里常和「不受暑」连在一起 —— 因为不易褪，夏天的衣服爱用它。倒是栀子花本身是白的，跟这个颜色没有关系：栀黄说的是果实，不是花。
items.funEn: Gardenia served as medicine, as incense and as dyestuff all at once. The yellow it yields is repeatedly associated in old texts with summer clothing, on the grounds that it holds up in heat and light. The flower, meanwhile, is white; the colour takes its name from the fruit and has nothing to do with the blossom.

items.histZh: 柘黄是从柘树的木料里提取的染料染成的黄，隋唐以后逐渐专供帝王，「柘袍」在诗文里直接就是皇帝的代称。它的色相比后来定型的明黄要沉一些，偏赤。从唐代起，庶民禁用这类黄色，从此黄与皇权牢牢绑在一起。屏幕上的柘黄按唐宋文献的记载复原，真实程度有限。
items.histEn: Zhe yellow came from dye extracted from the wood of the zhe tree, a kind of silkworm thorn, and from the Sui and Tang onward it was increasingly reserved for the throne — the phrase zhe robe simply means the emperor. It sits deeper and redder than the bright imperial yellow that was later codified. From the Tang, commoners were forbidden to wear such yellows, and from then on the colour and the crown were fastened together. The value here is a reconstruction from Tang and Song descriptions.
items.funZh: 柘树本身是养蚕用的：古人用柘叶喂蚕，出的丝叫「柘丝」，比桑蚕丝更韧。所以柘黄从一棵养蚕的树上来，最后穿在了皇帝身上 —— 一条从蚕房到朝堂的路径，全靠一棵树连着。
items.funEn: The zhe tree was grown to feed silkworms; its leaves produced a tougher thread than mulberry silk. So the imperial yellow arrived from a tree kept for sericulture, and travelled from the rearing shed to the throne room along a single branch.

items.histZh: 韭黄不是染料色，是食材色 —— 韭菜在不见光的窖里长出来，叶绿素来不及生成，于是通体淡黄。古人冬天用「黄芽」法在窖中催生菜蔬，韭黄是其中最讲究的一样，宋人笔记里写它「色淡黄，味极嫩」。这个颜色因此在传统色里显得格外轻，几乎是一种「没有晒过太阳的绿」。
items.histEn: This is a vegetable rather than a dye — chives grown in the dark, where chlorophyll never forms and the whole plant comes out pale yellow. Chinese households forced vegetables in cellars through the winter, and blanched chives were the most prized of them; Song dynasty notebooks describe the result as pale yellow and extremely tender. The colour is consequently among the lightest in the traditional palette, a green that has never met the sun.
items.funZh: 韭黄是「驯服光照」的产物：同一棵韭菜，见光就是深绿，遮光就是淡黄，中间的差别全在叶绿素有没有机会合成。把光这一段掐掉，植物就只能把养分堆在细胞里，于是更嫩、更甜。
items.funEn: Blanched chives are what happens when you interrupt light. The same plant is deep green exposed and pale yellow covered, and everything in between comes down to whether chlorophyll ever got the chance to form. Deny it the light and the plant simply piles its sugars into the cells, which is why it comes out sweeter and more tender.

items.histZh: 柳绿取早春柳芽初绽时的颜色，是黄绿里最嫩的一档。汉语里「柳绿桃红」连用，几乎是春景的固定搭配，明清的仕女画和瓷器纹样里常见这一对。它的黄多绿少，所以显得轻，和盛夏那种浓绿完全不是一回事。屏幕上的柳绿按新芽取色，柳叶长成后一周内就会明显转深。
items.histEn: Willow green is the colour of a willow bud just beginning to open in early spring — the palest and tenderest of the yellow-greens. Chinese couples willow green with peach red as a fixed formula for spring scenery, and the pairing turns up constantly in Ming and Qing figure painting and on porcelain. There is more yellow in it than green, which keeps it light; it is nothing like the solid green of high summer. This sample is from a newly opened bud; inside a week the leaf turns noticeably darker.
items.funZh: 柳芽的黄绿只维持很短一段：同一根枝条，先出的芽最黄，几天后新叶展开就转成真正的绿。所以「柳绿」这个词天生带着时间感，说的是某几天的颜色，不是一整个季节的颜色。
items.funEn: The yellow-green of a willow lasts only days. On a single branch the earliest buds are the yellowest, and once the leaves open the colour resolves into a plain green. Willow green therefore carries a date inside it — it names a handful of days rather than a season.

items.histZh: 葱绿取自葱叶，是清亮的黄绿，比柳绿更饱和、更偏冷一点。它在传统色里属于常用档，衣服、窗纱、瓷釉都用得上。清代宫廷档案里记过「葱绿」染料的配比，是少数能在文献里查到方子的色名之一。屏幕上的葱绿偏鲜，实际植物染要灰一些，染坊常靠套染来回调。
items.histEn: Scallion green comes from the leaf of the scallion: a clear yellow-green, more saturated and a shade cooler than willow. It was a working colour in the traditional palette, used on clothing, window gauze and glazes. Qing palace archives record dye recipes by the name, making it one of the relatively few traditional shades whose formula survives in documents. This value is fresher than reality; plant dye comes out greyer, and dyers adjusted it by overdyeing.
items.funZh: 传统色里有一批「蔬菜色」：葱绿、韭黄、豆绿、蟹壳青、鸭卵青。它们不是画家调出来的，是从厨房里长出来的词。这类色名的好处是所有人都见过实物，不必解释 —— 说「葱绿」，对方脑子里立刻有一个具体的亮度。
items.funEn: A whole family of traditional names comes straight out of the kitchen: scallion green, chive yellow, pea green, crab-shell blue-green, duck-egg blue. These are not colours a painter mixed but words that grew where vegetables did. Their advantage is that everyone has seen the object, so no explanation is required — say scallion green and the other party already has a specific brightness in mind.

items.histZh: 苹果绿取青苹果表皮的颜色，比葱绿深、比草绿亮，是黄绿里偏中段的一档。苹果在中国是后来才普及的果品，所以这个色名比「葱绿」「柳绿」晚得多，大体上是近世才定型的。屏幕上的苹果绿按未熟果取色，熟透的果子会转黄转红，同一颗上下的颜色也不一样。
items.histEn: Apple green is taken from the skin of an unripe apple — deeper than scallion green, brighter than grass, sitting in the middle of the yellow-green band. Apples became a commonplace fruit in China comparatively late, so this name is much younger than scallion or willow, settling into the vocabulary only in recent centuries. The sample comes from a fruit not yet ripe; as it matures the skin shifts yellow and then red, and no two patches on one apple match.
items.funZh: 「以水果命名颜色」是传统色里最能作弊的一招：谁都知道苹果绿大概是什么样，不必定义饱和度和明度。代价是它随品种、产地、成熟度浮动极大 —— 同一句苹果绿，青苹和奶油苹果能差出小半档明度。
items.funEn: Naming a colour after a fruit is the cheapest trick in the book: everyone knows roughly what apple green looks like, and nobody has to define saturation or lightness. The cost is that it drifts enormously with variety, origin and ripeness — the same two words can cover a difference of half a step in lightness between a Granny Smith and a Cream apple.

items.histZh: 韭绿是韭菜叶子的绿，比葱绿更黄、更嫩，是黄绿里偏亮的一档。韭菜在中国栽培极早，《诗经》里就有「献羔祭韭」，是把韭菜当祭品的年代，后来才慢慢变成日常菜蔬。韭绿和韭黄恰好是一对：同一株植物，见光是绿，遮光是黄。屏幕上的韭绿按春韭取色，夏韭要深得多。
items.histEn: Chive green is the colour of the leaf itself: yellower and tenderer than scallion, one of the brighter yellow-greens. Chives were cultivated in China remarkably early — the Book of Songs mentions presenting lamb and chives as an offering, a time when the plant was sacrificial before it was everyday. Chive green and chive yellow make a matched pair from one plant: exposed to light it is green, covered it is yellow. This sample is spring chives; the summer growth runs much darker.
items.funZh: 韭菜割了又长，是「一茬一茬」这个说法的来源之一，古人因此把它看成生机不断的象征。颜色上它也分了层次：头茬最嫩最黄，割过几茬之后叶色会一点点变深变硬，同一块地里前后能出好几个绿。
items.funEn: Chives regrow after cutting, which is part of where Chinese gets its idiom for crop after crop, and the plant became a small emblem of inexhaustible life. The colour keeps that record too: the first cutting is the tenderest and yellowest, and with each regrowth the leaves darken and toughen, so one patch yields several distinguishable greens across a season.

items.histZh: 艾绿取艾叶背面的颜色，是蒙了一层白霜的灰绿，比正经的植物绿闷得多。艾草在中国节令里位置很高：端午悬艾、艾灸治病，都很早，所以艾绿是个带药用气味的色名。它的灰不是脏，是叶片表面那层绒毛造成的 —— 摸上去也是这个手感。屏幕上的艾绿按鲜叶取色。
items.histEn: Mugwort green is the underside of a mugwort leaf: a greyed green wearing a coat of bloom, far duller than a healthy plant green. Mugwort sits high in the Chinese ritual calendar — hung on doors at the Dragon Boat Festival, burned in moxibustion — so the colour word carries the smell of medicine. Its greyness is not dirt but the fine hairs on the leaf surface, which is also what you feel when you touch it. This sample is from a fresh leaf.
items.funZh: 艾绿的灰来自结构而不是颜料：叶面绒毛把入射光散掉一部分，反射回来的颜色就淡了。很多「植物带霜的绿」都是这个成因，比如葡萄皮、蓝莓、荷叶背面的白粉 —— 也是同一类物理效果，不是长了什么东西。
items.funEn: The grey in mugwort green comes from structure rather than pigment: hairs on the leaf scatter part of the incoming light, and what returns is washed out. Many bloomy plant greens work the same way — grape skins, blueberries, the whitish film on the underside of a lotus leaf. It is a physical effect, not a coating that has grown there.

items.histZh: 官绿是明清染作里的一档标准色，名字里的「官」指的正是官方定样 —— 由官营染署给出布样，民间照染。它比草绿更蓝、更沉，常用来染官服的下摆、仪仗和帐幕。官绿、官青一类带「官」字的色名，本质上是当时的国家标准色卡，作用跟今天的潘通差不多。
items.histEn: Official green was a standard shade of the Ming and Qing dye workshops, and the word official in its name is literal: state dye offices issued the swatch and private workshops matched it. Bluer and heavier than grass green, it went onto the hems of official dress, into processional gear and onto tenting. Names carrying the word official — official green, official blue — were effectively the national standard colour card of their day, doing much the same job as a modern Pantone chip.
items.funZh: 古代也有「色卡」这回事：官营作坊定样之后会把布样发下去，各地照染再交上来验收。麻烦在于天然染料批次之间总有偏差，于是文献里常见「色浅」「色深」被退回去重染的记录 —— 标准化这件事，从来都要靠一整套流程兜着。
items.funEn: Standard colour cards are not a modern invention. State workshops issued swatches, local dyers matched them and the cloth came back for inspection. Because natural dyes vary batch to batch, the archives are full of rejected pieces marked too pale or too dark and sent back for another pass. Standardisation has always depended on process, not on the chip alone.

items.histZh: 苔绿取苔藓的颜色，是黄绿里最灰、最暗的一档，几乎是黄绿和橄榄色的交界。中国园林里苔是正经的观赏对象，「苔痕上阶绿」这类句子把苔写成了时间本身 —— 有苔说明这地方够老、够静。屏幕上的苔绿按阴湿处的苔取色，向阳面的苔会黄得多。
items.histEn: Moss green is the colour of moss: the greyest and darkest of the yellow-greens, sitting almost exactly on the border with olive. In Chinese gardens moss was a legitimate object of appreciation, and lines about moss creeping green across the steps treat it as a visible form of time — moss means the place is old enough and quiet enough. This sample comes from moss in damp shade; in sun it yellows considerably.
items.funZh: 苔没有真正的根，靠表面吸水，所以长得极慢，几厘米厚可能要好几年。这也是园林里那句「苔痕上阶绿」的底气：苔痕不是一天长出来的，它记的是无人走动的年月。
items.funEn: Moss has no true roots and takes water across its surface, which is why it grows so slowly — a few centimetres may represent years. That is what gives the garden line about moss on the steps its weight. The green is not something that appeared overnight; it is a record of the years nobody walked there.

items.histZh: 螺子黛是古代画眉用的墨，产自波斯一带，因为呈螺形得名，色是偏蓝的灰黑。它在唐代属于极贵重的进口品，颜师古注《隋书》时专门说过它「出波斯国，每颗值十金」。用它画出来的眉不是纯黑，而是带一层青灰，所以这个色名其实介于黑与蓝紫之间。屏幕上的螺子黛是按墨色推的近似值。
items.histEn: Luozi dai was the ink Chinese women used to paint their eyebrows, imported from Persia and named for its spiral shape; the colour is a blue-leaning grey-black. In the Tang it was a luxury import, expensive enough that a commentator annotating the Sui history felt obliged to note that a single piece cost ten times its weight in gold. Eyebrows drawn with it were never flat black but carried a blue-grey film, which is why the colour word sits between black and blue-violet. The value shown is inferred from ink.
items.funZh: 古人画眉的墨不只一种，贫富有别：有钱用螺子黛，次一等用铜黛，再往下就用普通的石墨甚至烧焦的柳枝。一套眉毛用品能排出四五档价格，跟今天口红的档次分层几乎是同一个逻辑。
